page: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a legacy generation, storage-optimized virtual instance running on the Xen hypervisor. The hardware profile is built around an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 dedicated vCPUs distributed across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by 25 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 122.0 GB of RAM, equating to 7.62 GB per virtual core. Storage includes 3,200 GB of bundled local solid-state drive capacity, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance does not include graphical acceleration hardware.

Benchmark results highlight the age and architecture of the underlying Ivy Bridge generation CPU. Raw per-core execution speeds are comparatively low, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 532.0 and text processing score of 1080.0, both falling into the bottom 10 percent of recorded systems. Multi-core performance is mixed, with stress-ng registering 14125.68 in the middle tier, whereas Geekbench multi-core performance places in the lower 25 percent at 3448.0. Large-block uncached memory write throughput measures 18.74 GB/sec, also in the lower quartile, though small cached reads maintain solid throughput at 588.91 GB/sec.

Data handling benchmarks show steady operational capability in legacy storage-centric contexts, reaching 6.04 million Redis SET operations per second and 14.27 GB/sec static web serving throughput. However, compute-heavy tasks like LLM prompt evaluation and decompression struggle relative to modern hardware classes. From an operational efficiency perspective, the platform delivers significant local NVMe-precursor SSD capacity and substantial RAM density, but yields poor compute output per core relative to newer architecture tiers.

Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is targeted toward I/O-intensive workloads requiring large amounts of direct-attached solid-state storage and memory footprint without modern instruction-set extensions. Practical workloads include intermediate NoSQL data stores, caching layers, log analysis, and transactional database operational nodes where throughput is bounded by local drive capacity rather than modern CPU throughput.
description: Amazon Web Services i2.4xlarge is a storage-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Configured on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 16 dedicated vCPUs across 8 physical cores, 122.0 GB of memory, and 3,200 GB of bundled local SSD storage, backed by a baseline network throughput of 2 Gbps. Lacking hardware GPU accelerators, the instance relies on legacy CPU instructions. Benchmark data indicates modest single-thread and multi-thread processing speeds, placing low in modern compute evaluations, while maintaining average throughput in localized database operations and static data transfer. Memory capacity and bundled local storage are high relative to the virtual core allocation, making the hardware profile suited to legacy database operations, caching nodes, and high-capacity storage workloads that prioritize local solid-state capacity over intense central processing unit performance.
